defect_observations: Source locators checked in the author version: p.15 (Section 8 A Dynamic View: f_A, irrational domain, continuity argument, Sp(A), K4/K5 examples, finite-spectrum conjecture continued on p.16) and pp.16-18 (Section 9: K_{3,k}, threshold n^{-1/3-1/k}, N(x1,x2,x3), EVEN, BIGGER, A*, R_u, Representation Lemma with l<k/3, T_alpha and counting outlines, u1,u2 and u1..u4 enlargement, almost sure encoding notion, Hella-Kolaitis-Luosto problem); p.7 has the sample exponent alpha=pi/7; Generic Extension at p.10. All match the cited content.

The chapter follows the author's 30-page version and says so (body 32-50, 519-526; own bib entry Spencer2007LogicRandomStructuresAuthor whose note states locators refer to the author version). The printed Springer chapter is not consulted; accepted under the 2026-10-11 version directive.

Scope note, not a coverage gap: the source says A* has all 1/3+1/k as spectral points and that the encoded A 'has the desired infinite spectrum'. The chapter proves the A* claim on [1/3,1) and proves A has infinite spectrum with Sp(A) on [1/3,1/2) equal to {1/3} u {1/3+1/k : k>=7}; it states (body 416-430) that f_A on I_k for k<=5 and the point 1/2 are not determined, and proves the source's Representation Lemma fails for l=1 when k in {4,5} (body 302-315, annex 433-475). A reviewer may decide whether 'desired' should be read as all 1/3+1/k for A.

The transfer of the almost sure Representation Lemma into T_alpha (body 295-300) relies on completeness of T_alpha with all members holding almost surely, taken from thm:p03-w03-p03-065-shelah-spencer (packet 065); it is not reproved here and is not needed by the chapter's own proofs.
